# F1: config re-declare and class inheritance {#sec-fg-config-redeclare}

A class re-declare overrides a vanilla engine class at load time. This page
states the re-declare that works, the re-declare that fails, the engine
limits, and the visible defect a wrong value shows. Read the engine config
first, then restate the real parent {src:pbo:Dta/bin.pbo}.

## What works

A re-declare that repeats the class name and its parent merges the named
values. Every inherited field survives. The engine merge is per property
{src:adr:ADR-027}.

AEE uses this form. Inside `CfgWorlds` it re-declares `DOFPars`,
`DayLightingBrightAlmost` and `DayLightingRainy`, each with its own name as
the parent {src:script:addons/lighting/config.cpp}. The engine keeps the
vanilla keyframes and the AEE values win {src:cfg:CfgWorlds>>DefaultWorld}.

The parent restatement rule governs every re-declare. You name the real
engine parent of a vanilla class. A test fails any re-declare that omits the
parent {src:script:tools/tests/test_config_inheritance.py}.

`requiredAddons[]` sets the load order. AEE declares its dependencies in the
list, so the engine loads them before AEE and the AEE values win
{src:script:addons/actions/config.cpp}. The base game always loads first, so
every AEE re-declare wins over the base game {src:cfg:CfgPatches>>requiredAddons}.

A forward declaration sits at the nested scope that uses it. AEE declares
`class Default;` inside `CfgCloudlets` before the child class
{src:script:addons/particles/config.cpp}. The declaration resolves the name
and does not shadow the vanilla base {src:cfg:CfgCloudlets>>Default}.

## What does not work

A class with no parent drops every inherited value. The engine strips the
fields and logs `Updating base class '<parent>'->''` {src:cfg:CfgMarkers}.
This defect produced `No entry CfgMarkers/*.scope` and `Wrong location draw
style` in the AEE RPT {src:adr:ADR-027}.

A file-root forward declaration is a trap. `class Y;` at column zero makes
the engine create an empty class Y and re-parent the existing entries onto
it. The real definition is destroyed. AEE forbids a file-root declaration of
the world classes {src:script:tools/tests/test_config_inheritance.py}.

An override of a key AEE does not own is a defect. A generated header
disowns the keys that thermal and optics own, because a second declaration
wins and changes the model {src:script:addons/vehicles/generated/CfgVehicles.hpp}.
Name only the fields you own, so the engine values survive {src:adr:ADR-001}.

## Limitations

Config is load-time and global. A config merges into the engine tree when the
PBO loads. The merge is last-loaded-wins per property {src:adr:ADR-027}. No
script command writes the config tree for these classes. The PBO is the only
off switch {src:adr:ADR-001}.

Load order over an undeclared mod cannot be guaranteed. Only the mod-list
order decides that merge. AEE detects and logs it instead of chasing it
{src:adr:ADR-027}.

The engine C++ runtime is closed. The simulation solver, the renderer and
the flight model are not addressable by config or by script {src:adr:ADR-031}.

## Breaks visually

A wrong material or a wrong hidden-selection index corrupts the picture. A
per-selection material swap on the wrong selection alters the visible
appearance. This is the Zulu uniform defect, issue #123 {src:adr:ADR-001}.

The selection number is an index, not a name. `setObjectMaterial` takes the
number from the `hiddenSelections[]` array in the vehicle config, and the
index starts at 0 {src:cmd:setObjectMaterial}. An index that is off by one
paints the wrong part of the model {src:cfg:CfgVehicles>>hiddenSelectionsMaterials}.
